sections.content: How many people are "archivists, conservators and curators"?

9,380 people

were counted on the census as "archivists, conservators and curators" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Archivists, conservators and curators collect, appraise and preserve collections of recorded and other material of historical interest.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 35 to 39 years. Of the whole working population 11.5% were aged 35 to 39 years. For people working as "archivists, conservators and curators", 14% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "archivists, conservators and curators" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "archivists, conservators and curators" included:

  • managers and directors in retail and wholesale
  • construction and building trades supervisors
  • barristers and judges

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "archivists, conservators and curators" there were more women than men (65.8% compared with 34.2%).

This means "archivists, conservators and curators" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business, media and public service professionals".

Men made up 34.2% and women made up 65.8% of "archivists, conservators and curators"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "archivists, conservators and curators" included:

  • veterinarians
  • education advisers and school inspectors
  • legal professionals (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "archivists, conservators and curators" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "archivists, conservators and curators" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "archivists, conservators and curators", 12.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (64.7% compared with 35.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (82.5%) than self-employed (17.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Hackney, this is in the same region of London.
